ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. If the guide words are 'farm' and 'feast', which word is on that page? (1 mark)
   A. fashion
   B. mango
   C. zebra
   D. apple

2. Which sentence uses 'the' correctly for a best one? (1 mark)
   A. She is the tallest girl.
   B. She is tall the girl.
   C. She is tallest a girl.
   D. She is a the tallest girl.

3. Which is safe when filling an online form? (1 mark)
   A. Give your password to any site
   B. Fill it in secret
   C. Share your address with strangers
   D. Fill it with a parent or teacher

4. Which pair is a minimal pair for /l/ and /r/? (1 mark)
   A. lake, rake
   B. boy, toy
   C. five, nine
   D. bird, girl

5. Poems and similes: Which is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. She sang.
   B. She sang loudly.
   C. She sang like a bird.
   D. She is a bird.

6. Which word stays the same in the plural? (1 mark)
   A. hen
   B. sheep
   C. cow
   D. goat

7. 'She reads a lot.' Here 'a lot' means (1 mark)
   A. never
   B. often or much
   C. only one book
   D. a place

8. In the word 'hospital', which syllable is stressed? (1 mark)
   A. The first
   B. The second
   C. The third
   D. None

9. Which word starts with the cluster 'sn'? (1 mark)
   A. snake
   B. treatment
   C. stop
   D. stitch

10. Where does the sender's address go in a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. In the middle
   B. At the bottom left
   C. After the name
   D. At the top right

11. Listening and diet: Which word has the long sound /uː/? (1 mark)
   A. good
   B. book
   C. foot
   D. food

12. Which is a minimal pair for /f/ and /v/? (1 mark)
   A. book, look
   B. jam, ham
   C. safe, save
   D. pen, pin

13. Which is a way of choosing a book? (1 mark)
   A. Choose the biggest only
   B. Read the title, cover and first page
   C. Choose a book with no words
   D. Choose the one nobody likes

14. Which is an example of extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Writing a letter
   B. Learning a poem for an exam
   C. Reading one line for a test
   D. Reading many story books in your free time

15. Adjectives: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. This is beautifuller than that.
   B. This is more beautifuler than that.
   C. This is beautifullest than that.
   D. This is more beautiful than that.

16. To reply to a message means to (1 mark)
   A. delete it
   B. answer it
   C. forward it only
   D. ignore it

17. 'Steal' means to (1 mark)
   A. read a book
   B. give a gift
   C. wash clothes
   D. take something that does not belong to you

18. Quantifiers: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. I do not any have money.
   B. I do not have any money.
   C. I do not have many money.
   D. I do not have some money.

19. Which sentence is in the past tense? (1 mark)
   A. Baraka will click Send.
   B. Baraka clicks Send.
   C. Baraka is clicking Send.
   D. Baraka clicked Send.

20. Choose the correct -ing form of 'make'. (1 mark)
   A. makking
   B. maiking
   C. makeing
   D. making

21. Which question is factual? (1 mark)
   A. How did Omondi feel deep inside?
   B. Who told Baraka about how HIV spreads?
   C. Why do you think Baraka is brave?
   D. What lesson does the story teach?

22. Which is the adverb form of 'happy'? (1 mark)
   A. happly
   B. happily
   C. happyly
   D. happiy

23. Which is a nonverbal cue that shows you are listening? (1 mark)
   A. Talking to a friend
   B. Looking out of the window
   C. Turning your back
   D. Looking at the speaker and nodding

24. Which word has the short vowel /ɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. feel
   B. seat
   C. live
   D. leave

25. Which conjunction shows a difference? 'The water looked clean, ____ it was not safe.' (1 mark)
   A. but
   B. and
   C. or
   D. so

26. Choose the word that means 'to listen with your ears'. (1 mark)
   A. here
   B. heer
   C. hair
   D. hear

27. How is a diary different from a letter? (1 mark)
   A. A diary always has an address
   B. A diary is always sent by post
   C. A diary is written for yourself and is not sent
   D. A diary has no date

28. Which sentence describes a feeling? (1 mark)
   A. We swept the paths.
   B. It was Saturday.
   C. We planted five trees.
   D. I felt proud of our work.

29. What is a byline? (1 mark)
   A. The price of the paper
   B. The name of the writer of an article
   C. An advert
   D. A picture

30. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'glad'? (1 mark)
   A. happpy
   B. hapie
   C. hapy
   D. happy

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. List three things you can do to remember what you have read. (3 marks)

32. Explain what we learn from the story about honesty. (3 marks)

33. Copy in neat print: 'Please listen carefully.' Circle the silent letter. (2 marks)

34. Explain the difference in position of 'enough' with a noun and with an adjective. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

35. Name the three groups of food on a healthy plate and give one example of each. (3 marks)

36. Replace each plain word with a better describing word: nice room, dirty clothes, good smell. Write the new phrases. (3 marks)

37. Write two words for each cluster: (a) br (b) gr. (4 marks)

38. List the three parts of a narrative and say what each tells. (3 marks)

39. Write a title and an opening sentence for a story about a girl who finds a lost phone. (2 marks)

40. Put the adjectives in the right order: a (red, round, big) balloon. (2 marks)

41. Give one riddle about an object used for cleaning, with its answer. (2 marks)

42. Write one sentence in the present progressive and one in the past progressive about a farm. (4 marks)

43. Write three sentences you would say to report an accident to an adult. (3 marks)

44. What kind of person is Kamau in 'The Clean-Up Day'? Give a reason from the text. (3 marks)

45. Write a narrative of about 60 words about a visit to a shop. Use one simile and two time words. (5 marks)

46. Write a short dialogue of four lines between two learners about sending an email. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — fashion
   Fashion comes after farm and before feast in the alphabet.

2. A — She is the tallest girl.
   We use the before superlative words such as tallest.

3. D — Fill it with a parent or teacher
   A trusted adult can help you keep your details safe.

4. A — lake, rake
   Lake and rake differ only in the first sound.

5. C — She sang like a bird.
   Like a bird compares her singing to a bird's.

6. B — sheep
   Sheep is both singular and plural.

7. B — often or much
   A lot at the end of a sentence tells how much or how often.

8. A — The first
   We say HOS-pi-tal.

9. A — snake
   Snake starts with s and n.

10. D — At the top right
   Address and date are at the top right.

11. D — food
   Food has /uː/. The others have /ʊ/.

12. C — safe, save
   They differ in the last sound.

13. B — Read the title, cover and first page
   These clues show whether the book interests you.

14. D — Reading many story books in your free time
   Extensive reading means reading widely.

15. D — This is more beautiful than that.
   Long adjectives use more.

16. B — answer it
   To reply is to answer.

17. D — take something that does not belong to you
   Stealing is taking what is not yours.

18. B — I do not have any money.
   Use any in negative sentences.

19. D — Baraka clicked Send.
   Clicked is the past form.

20. D — making
   Verbs ending in silent e drop the e before -ing.

21. B — Who told Baraka about how HIV spreads?
   A factual question has its answer stated in the text.

22. B — happily
   Change y to i and add -ly.

23. D — Looking at the speaker and nodding
   Eye contact and nods show attention.

24. C — live
   'Live' has a short /ɪ/.

25. A — but
   'But' shows contrast.

26. D — hear
   'Hear' is what we do with our ears.

27. C — A diary is written for yourself and is not sent
   A letter is sent to another person.

28. D — I felt proud of our work.
   'Proud' is a feeling.

29. B — The name of the writer of an article
   A byline says who wrote the article.

30. D — happy
   Happy has a double p.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Write new words and meanings; say one sentence about each chapter; draw a story map; retell the story to a partner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct suggestion.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty means returning what belongs to others. Neema returned the purse and refused a reward, and her mother said honesty is a great treasure.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for the message.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Please listen carefully. (silent t in listen)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for neat copying and 1 mark for identifying t.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: With a noun, enough comes before it: enough food. With an adjective, enough comes after it: tall enough.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position and 1 mark for each example.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Energy foods such as ugali; body-building foods such as beans; protective foods such as spinach.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group with an example.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: bright, tidy room; muddy, crumpled clothes; fresh smell.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) bring, broom (or bread, brush) (b) green, grass (or grow, ground)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: who, where and when. Middle: the events. End: how it finished.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title: An Honest Girl. One morning, Achieng found a phone near the school gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: a big round red balloon
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for size first and 1 mark for shape before colour.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have hairs but no head, and I clean your teeth. What am I? A toothbrush.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a clear riddle and 1 for the correct answer.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The farmer is digging the field. The cows were eating grass.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each sentence: 1 for the correct form of be, 1 for the -ing verb.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Help! There is an emergency. A boy has fallen and his arm is bleeding. Please bring the first aid kit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clear sentence.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Observant and responsible: he noticed a hole in the fence and said it should be fixed at once.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality and 1 for evidence.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: A story of about 60 words with beginning, middle and end, one simile, two time words such as first and then, and correct punctuation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for beginning, events, simile, time words, and punctuation.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: A: How do we send an email? B: First click Compose. A: Now I type the address. B: Then write your message and press Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line with correct speaker format.
